documents.name: Nada Fighting Festival
documents.summary: Himeji’s famously physical autumn festival, where heavy mikoshi and yatai are carried, struck and manoeuvred in tightly packed ritual contests.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The collisions, massed carriers and physical force create an unusually visceral festival spectacle with a very different energy from decorative float processions.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The useful programme is concentrated and extremely crowded, and the intensity creates safety and sightline constraints for casual visitors.

visit-window.note: A fixed October festival; choose viewing areas conservatively and follow local crowd controls.

documents.name: Awaji Tadao Ando Architecture Circuit
documents.localName: 淡路島 安藤忠雄建築
documents.summary: A concentrated Awaji Island architecture circuit linking Tadao Ando’s vast Yumebutai landscape complex with the compact, intensely staged Honpukuji Water Temple.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The island lets architecture-focused visitors experience Ando’s concrete, water, light and landscape language across two genuinely different spatial scales in one coherent half- to full-day circuit.

booking.note: The two principal public sites do not form one reserved tour; verify current opening hours separately before building the circuit.

coreExperience.note: The core architectural experience is spatial and visual; Japanese is not required to appreciate either principal work.

mobility.note: Yumebutai is a large terraced landscape complex with extensive vertical circulation; visitors should not infer a compact two-building stop from the map.

multi-site.label: Two-site architecture circuit
multi-site.note: The MultiPoint geometry deliberately represents Yumebutai and Honpukuji Water Temple; transport between them is part of the visit.

weather.condition: Allow for substantial outdoor circulation at Yumebutai.
weather.note: The architecture is visitable year-round, but rain, summer heat and strong weather change the comfort of the landscape-heavy Yumebutai component.

documents.name: Iya Bijin
documents.summary: A rare case where exceptional gorge scenery and source-fed private bathing remain available at regional rather than luxury-brand prices.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A rare case where exceptional gorge scenery and source-fed private bathing remain available at regional rather than luxury-brand prices.
cardSignals: Two: Published reference rates are about ¥37,800–47,800 total for two in standard rooms and about ¥67,800 in the detached two bath suite, with half board.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor bath is guaranteed in every room; choose the detached suite for maximum privacy.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: The source is a cool sulfur/mineral spring and is heated; published reference prices need live confirmation.

documents.name: Shiki no Sato Hanamura
documents.localName: 小田温泉 四季の里 はなむら
documents.summary: Detached accommodation and private bathing reach unusually accessible prices in a quieter alternative to Kurokawa.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Detached accommodation and private bathing reach unusually accessible prices in a quieter alternative to Kurokawa.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥45,000–60,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Book an outdoor-bath category; not every room type qualifies.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Official disclosure indicates a combined flow/circulation system with added water; do not describe it as pristine kakenagashi.

documents.name: Funamachi
documents.summary: The ultra-soft, egg-rich texture and dashi dipping make authentic akashiyaki structurally different from takoyaki despite superficial similarity.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Akashi's soft egg-rich dumpling eaten with clear dashi. The recommended visit is: Order one tray, taste plain first, then dip briefly in dashi without letting every piece collapse.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Small shop; queues, irregular holidays and sold-out closure possible.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Just before opening on a weekday

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: C: simple order but queue/rules need preparation

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Good from Akashi Station with walk

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Small seating; order expectations and photography rules should be observed.

documents.name: Arakiya
documents.summary: Warigo serving and dark, aromatic flour connect soba technique with Izumo pilgrimage travel rather than presenting a generic zaru set.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Dark whole-buckwheat soba served in stacked warigo boxes. The recommended visit is: Order warigo first and move condiments/sauce between tiers as instructed.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Peak shrine days can produce long waits and early sell-out.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Sauce is reused progressively across boxes; ask if uncertain.

documents.name: Saijo Festival
documents.summary: A group of shrine festivals in Saijo involving more than a hundred danjiri, mikoshi and taikodai, including a dramatic river procession.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The sheer number of floats and the Kamo River climax give Saijo exceptional density and scale among Shikoku’s autumn festivals.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The programme is dispersed across multiple shrines and days, and some experiential overlap with other elite float festivals reduces its singularity.

visit-window.note: Multiple shrine festivals unfold across October; choose the exact procession and date before travel.

documents.name: Anagomeshi Ueno Miyajimaguchi Honten
documents.localName: あなごめしうえの 宮島口本店
documents.summary: The concentrated eel stock rice and grilled anago retain the logic of a travel bento while rewarding a sit-down comparison at the original route node.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Char-grilled conger eel rice developed for Miyajima-bound travellers. The recommended visit is: Reserve dine-in if possible, or pre-order the bento and eat at a suitable point in the journey.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Very high demand; dine-in and takeaway procedures differ.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Takeaway pickup times and dine-in queue rules are separate.

documents.name: Tea Culture Hall
documents.summary: A surprisingly rich public tea centre in mountain Hoshino where gyokuro can be experienced through concentrated shizuku-cha, grinding, whisking and tea-based food rather than a single cup.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It offers multiple levels of engagement—from an inexpensive tasting to more deliberate tea practice—without requiring specialist Japanese or a private farm appointment.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Free entry; tea, meals and experiences generally ¥500–3,000

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Current official/social information lists 10:00–17:00, generally Tuesday closure with seasonal and holiday exceptions; check the calendar.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: April–May around new tea, or a quiet weekday outside festivals.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Some visitor-oriented support may exist; machine translation is sufficient for most experiences.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Entry and basic tea service usually walk-in; selected experiences and private tea-room plans require reservation

legacy-visit-duration.label: Visit duration
legacy-visit-duration.note: 1–2 hours; longer with a meal or reserved room

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible by long bus journey, but a car is much more practical in Hoshino

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Gyokuro service has a sequence; follow staff guidance and do not drink all water as one ordinary large cup.

documents.name: Awa Odori Kaikan
documents.summary: A year-round home for Tokushima’s Awa Odori where skilled dance performances, a museum and audience participation turn a seasonal festival into an accessible permanent experience.
documents.whyWorthwhile: An excellent compact cultural experience for visitors who will not be in Tokushima during the main August festival. It is not a full-day destination and spoken explanation is mostly Japanese, but the dance is visually immediate and participation travels well across language barriers.

audience.notes: The visual performance is broadly accessible; very young children may not sustain interest through a full show and museum visit.

coverImage.alt: Awa Odori Kaikan building in Tokushima.

documents.name: Hirasei at Kintaikyo
documents.localName: 錦帯橋たもと ひらせい
documents.summary: The geometric, layered sushi reflects feast-scale production and local ingredients rather than the bite-size nigiri model familiar to most visitors.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Large-format layered pressed sushi associated with Iwakuni. The recommended visit is: Order a set centred on Iwakuni-zushi and lotus root.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Lunch-focused service; current venue/address should be checked because historical listings can confuse old and current sites.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Large sushi portions can be filling; order accordingly.

documents.name: Oku Takeo Onsen Kaze no Mori
documents.localName: 奥武雄温泉 風の森
documents.summary: A couples-only forest model with genuine detachment, thoughtful modern design and strong food.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A couples-only forest model with genuine detachment, thoughtful modern design and strong food.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥84,000–140,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor onsen is guaranteed in every two-person villa.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Kakenagashi/treatment was not clearly disclosed; carts, steps, insects and wildlife are part of the forest setting.

documents.name: Kaneda Castle + Shiratake
documents.summary: A seventh-century mountain fortress overlooking Asō Bay pairs with Tsushima's sacred quartz-porphyry summit for an unusually strong history-and-landscape combination.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Together they explain how Tsushima's border-island terrain shaped defence, religion and settlement. Kaneda provides archaeological depth and bay views; Shiratake adds the sharper physical and scenic climax.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: ancient mountain fortress walk · sacred mountain hike

coverImage.alt: Ancient stone defensive wall at Kaneda Castle on Tsushima.

documents.name: Kunisaki Minemichi Long Trail
documents.localName: 国東半島峯道ロングトレイル
documents.summary: Old ascetic paths link cave temples, cliff Buddhas, volcanic rock, farm basins and village roads into a sacred cultural landscape that works best as selected sections.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Few routes integrate geology, active religious heritage and lived rural landscape as densely. T1 is the clearest introduction; more rugged sections around T4/K1 add stronger ascetic atmosphere.

coverImage.alt: Rock-carved Dainichi Nyorai at Kumano Magaibutsu on the Kunisaki Peninsula.

documents.name: Oki Islands
documents.summary: A remote Sea of Japan archipelago combining giant sea cliffs, volcanic geology, grasslands, island culture and multi-day exploration.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The combination of Kuniga Coast scale, unusual geology and inhabited-island culture gives Oki enough breadth and singularity to justify building a separate island segment into a Japan trip.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Ferries, inter-island transport and weather make logistics substantial; the destination is poorly served by a rushed one-night visit.

visit-window.note: Sea conditions and seasonal transport influence inter-island plans; allow multiple days and schedule slack.

documents.name: Kawataro Yobuko
documents.summary: The meal demonstrates an unusually immediate handling chain: live squid becomes translucent sashimi, then remaining parts are cooked separately.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Yobuko live-squid sashimi and follow-up cooking of the body. The recommended visit is: Order the live-squid set and pay attention to texture before soy sauce dominates.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Catch and species depend on sea conditions; squid may be unavailable despite opening.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Moving tissue is expected; the second preparation should be requested/understood.

documents.name: Miune–Tenguzuka–Ushi-no-Se Ridge
documents.summary: Long open sasa ridges, isolated ponds and broad undeveloped horizons make the quieter western Tsurugi range a superb clear-weather day for a strong hiker.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Experienced Japanese hikers repeatedly singled out the western extension for solitude and sustained ridge quality rather than one summit. On a stable clear day it is a destination-worthy mountain journey.

coverImage.alt: Open mountain scenery around Miune in the western Tsurugi range.

documents.name: Ichiran no Mori Itoshima
documents.summary: It is useful not because Ichiran is obscure, but because the site exposes how a globally famous ramen chain engineers noodles, broth and customer flow.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Industrial-scale tonkotsu ramen production and chain system. The recommended visit is: Visit as an industrial food-system case study, then taste critically rather than assuming flagship superiority.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Reported 10:00–16:00; production viewing may not operate continuously.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Factory areas are viewed only from designated routes.

documents.name: Kamebishi-ya
documents.summary: The brewery preserves an unusually labour-intensive koji method and a dense historic production complex, but public access is less straightforward than at Yamaroku.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Rare mat-based koji making and long-aged soy sauce. The recommended visit is: Contact ahead for the most production-focused visit rather than relying on retail opening.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Unknown; retail low cost, tours/meal vary

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Visitor formats are limited and may be seasonal or appointment-based.

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Rail possible but local planning required

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Production access is appointment-controlled.

documents.name: Yoshinogari Historical Park
documents.summary: A vast reconstructed Yayoi-period moated settlement where archaeology is made tangible through buildings, landscape and hands-on ancient-life activities.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major regional destination and one of Japan’s strongest experiential archaeological sites. The large outdoor footprint is a virtue in mild weather but becomes a real heat, rain and walking consideration in summer.

audience.notes: School-age children gain the most from the craft and archaeology combination; younger children still have outdoor space but less historical comprehension.

coverImage.alt: Reconstructed northern inner-city gate at Yoshinogari Historical Park in Saga.

documents.name: Nagahama Fresh Fish Market Visitor Corridor
documents.localName: 長浜鮮魚市場 市場会館・見学者通路
documents.summary: The public corridor reveals the distribution infrastructure behind Fukuoka seafood, complementing restaurant consumption with an upstream view.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Fukuoka's wholesale seafood system and auction observation. The recommended visit is: Check auction timing, observe from the permitted corridor, then eat a species-specific breakfast/lunch in the market building.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Auction timing is early and workday-dependent; public access areas are limited.

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: No reservation for corridor; group visits may differ

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Remain in public corridors; do not obstruct workers or photograph where prohibited.

documents.name: Mizutaki Nagano
documents.summary: A disciplined, broth-first version of Hakata mizutaki where staff build the meal from concentrated chicken stock through meat, vegetables and final rice.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The meal is affordable relative to its depth and offers a regional hotpot experience more focused than many tourist-oriented alternatives.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Confirm course, party size, cancellation and final arrival time by phone.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Limited/unknown; set menu reduces ordering complexity.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: Preparation required because of Japanese telephone booking.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Arrive punctually; staff control cooking sequence.

documents.name: Yamaya Factory Terrace
documents.localName: やまやファクトリーテラス
documents.summary: The facility can make seasoning, maturation and industrial hygiene visible for a food often encountered only as a finished souvenir.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Modern cod-roe processing and Fukuoka mentaiko culture. The recommended visit is: Do the production route before tasting several seasoning levels; skip buying blindly by packaging.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Free self-guided areas; paid experiences/meal extra

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Cashless-only payment has been reported; production visibility depends on factory schedule.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Factory hygiene and viewing boundaries apply.

documents.name: Kominka Cafe Nagomi Oita
documents.localName: 古民家カフェ 和 大分店
documents.summary: Renovated traditional rural house serving elaborate toast, fruit desserts and cafe drinks.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The rural kominka setting and elaborate seasonal desserts are distinctive, but hours and review evidence remain weak.

documents.name: Kakiya
documents.summary: A rare single-ingredient restaurant that treats Hiroshima oysters through raw, grilled, fried and oil-marinated preparations without reducing them to tourist street food.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It provides a controlled comparison of one major regional ingredient in a convenient setting.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: The 2025–26 poor oyster crop affects supply; raw oysters and specific dishes may be unavailable or seasonal.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cool months normally strongest, but confirm current crop/supply.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Walk-in; limited reservation policy may apply

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: Shunpanro Shimonoseki Honten
documents.summary: The restaurant links technically demanding fugu preparation, Shimonoseki's port identity and the political history of the fish's legal rehabilitation.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Formal fugu cuisine in a historically central Shimonoseki institution. The recommended visit is: Reserve a full course that contrasts raw, cooked and broth preparations.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Seasonal course structure and private-room terms vary.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cooler months, lunch for easier comparison

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Licensed preparation; fixed-course and cancellation rules apply.

documents.name: Hozumitei
documents.summary: The dish demonstrates how one regional name can conceal two fundamentally different foodways: Uwajima's raw fish and egg sauce versus eastern Ehime's cooked rice.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Raw sea-bream-and-egg rice bowl distinct from cooked Matsuyama taimeshi. The recommended visit is: Order the Uwajima tai-meshi and one local fish-paste or seasonal fish side.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Dinner can be busy; lunch schedule should be checked.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Raw fish and egg are mixed into sauce/rice; follow house instructions.

documents.name: Yasuoka Kamaboko Jakoten-Making Experience
documents.localName: 安岡蒲鉾 じゃこ天作り体験
documents.summary: A concise producer workshop where whole small fish are transformed into Uwajima’s dark, textured jakoten rather than an anonymous smooth fish cake.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It turns an inexpensive station snack into a clear lesson in local fisheries, whole-fish use and texture.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Experience normally runs January–November, excluding Sundays, New Year and Obon; exact dates depend on production.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Any operating month; coordinate with rail timetable or a Uwajima drive.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: No English instructor guaranteed; the physical process is demonstrable with translation.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Required at least one week ahead

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Official producer or Ehime tourism booking/contact; 2–24 people, age five and older

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Practical near Futana Station, though regional trains are infrequent

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Follow hot-oil, hygiene and age instructions; children require supervision.

documents.name: Kuroshio Kobo
documents.summary: Visitors can see or perform the violent, aromatic straw sear that defines high-quality Kochi tataki rather than receiving an anonymous sliced plate.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Katsuo no tataki seared over burning rice straw at the fishing coast. The recommended visit is: Choose the straw-searing experience if operating, then eat the fish first with salt and aromatics before ponzu.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Bonito quality, weather and workshop availability are seasonal.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Spring first bonito or autumn returning bonito

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Fire safety instructions are mandatory; raw/seared interior is expected.

documents.name: Sanshu Izutsu Yashiki Wasanbon Workshop
documents.localName: 讃州井筒屋敷 和三盆型抜き体験
documents.summary: A low-barrier chance to press fine-grained local wasanbon sugar into traditional wooden moulds inside a preserved soy-sauce and sake merchant complex.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It combines edible craft, regional sugar history and a meaningful building without requiring a formal wagashi-school commitment.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Main-house admission ¥300; workshop roughly ¥1,000–1,500 depending current programme

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Official listing gives 10:00–16:00 and Wednesday closure; individual workshop days and prices should be reconfirmed.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Year-round; a good short stop when travelling the eastern Seto Inland Sea coast.

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Visual process is accessible; English explanation not guaranteed.

legacy-reservation-requirement.label: Reservation requirement
legacy-reservation-requirement.note: Often walk-in or same-day for individuals; groups should reserve

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Direct contact or on-site workshop desk; confirm current schedule

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Follow food-handling instructions and do not damage antique moulds or building areas.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Current workshop methods should be confirmed; carry cash.

documents.name: Jigoku Mushi Kobo Kannawa
documents.localName: 地獄蒸し工房 鉄輪
documents.summary: The visitor performs a real local cooking technique using the same geothermal system that structures Kannawa's bath and domestic culture.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Cooking ingredients in naturally hot geothermal steam. The recommended visit is: Buy a balanced basket including vegetables and one protein, then compare how steam changes sweetness and texture.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Steam-kettle fee from about ¥400 plus ingredients

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Reported 10:00–19:00 with third-Wednesday closure; verify current schedule and last kettle start.

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: No reservation; no reservation system reported

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Staff control kettle timing; steam causes severe burns, so follow every instruction.

documents.name: Uonotana Shopping Street
documents.summary: A compact working shopping street where Akashi octopus, sea bream and local ‘tamago-yaki’ can be sampled within the city’s fish trade.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The street is a strong area stop, especially when combined with the port and market history, but individual vendor quality varies.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Many fish retailers close earlier than restaurants; go before mid-afternoon.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Octopus and sea bream seasons add value; morning/lunch best.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: No unusual rule verified; confirm current house policy.

documents.name: TAO no Oka
documents.summary: DRUM TAO’s purpose-built outdoor theatre in the Kuju highlands, pairing taiko performance with wide mountain scenery.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The setting and high-energy ensemble make it one of Japan’s strongest permanent visual-performance stops and a memorable component of a Kuju itinerary.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The live segment is comparatively short and the remote location is substantial, so the experience is difficult to justify as a standalone long-distance detour.

visit-window.note: Performance dates and outdoor weather matter; sun, wind and rain protection may be needed.

documents.name: Gekkouju
documents.localName: 黒川温泉御処 月洸樹
documents.summary: Large suites, stars, forest and authentic water create one of Kurokawa’s strongest fully private models.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Large suites, stars, forest and authentic water create one of Kurokawa’s strongest fully private models.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥168,000–224,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Indoor and outdoor private baths are guaranteed in every detached suite.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Very expensive, and some baths use inward garden framing rather than long views.

documents.name: Takefue
documents.localName: 秘境 白川源泉 山荘 竹ふえ
documents.summary: Architecture, bamboo landscape, huge baths, authentic water and food produce a highly theatrical destination stay.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Architecture, bamboo landscape, huge baths, authentic water and food produce a highly theatrical destination stay.
cardSignals: Two: From roughly ¥206,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast; premium rooms can be substantially higher.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Book a room category explicitly showing the large outdoor source bath.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Extremely expensive and some baths prioritise enclosed garden privacy over broad natural views.

documents.name: Suganoya Ginza-dori
documents.localName: 菅乃屋 銀座通り店
documents.summary: A broad menu lets travellers compare cuts and cooking methods rather than reducing Kumamoto horse cuisine to one plate of red basashi.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Kumamoto horse-meat cuisine across raw and cooked preparations. The recommended visit is: Choose a cut-comparison basashi platter plus one cooked preparation.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Lunch/dinner menus differ; raw cuts can sell out.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Raw meat is optional; confirm cut names and origin.

documents.name: Motoyoshiya Honten
documents.localName: 元祖うなぎせいろむし 本吉屋 本店
documents.summary: Steaming the assembled eel and rice melds sauce, fat and grain differently from conventional unadon and belongs specifically to Yanagawa.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Yanagawa eel steamed with seasoned rice in a seiro box. The recommended visit is: Order the standard seiro-mushi; avoid adding a second eel preparation unless comparing techniques.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Reported 10:30–20:00, Monday closure; weekend/no-reservation conditions should be rechecked.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Weekday lunch, ideally with canal-town visit

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Official web/phone; weekend reservations may be restricted

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Seiro remains hot; reservations and queue differ by day.

documents.name: Ikeshima Coal-Mining Island
documents.summary: A still-inhabited former company town pairs a guided underground mine trolley experience with unusually direct surface access to Japan's postwar coal-mining landscape.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Hashima dominates the mining-island narrative, but Ikeshima offers more direct engagement with lived mining history. The underground experience is scheduled to end at the close of March 2027, making current planning time-critical.

coverImage.alt: Ikeshima’s dense former mining settlement and industrial structures seen from the island.

documents.name: Shokudo Kamecchi
documents.summary: A community-run demonstration of tamago-kake gohan built around local eggs, rice and condiments rather than a contrived luxury version.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It is extremely inexpensive and culturally revealing, though best treated as a regional stop rather than a major standalone detour.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Reopened August 3, 2026; verify the new operating calendar and any changed service system.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Raw egg consumption; follow refill and condiment rules posted on site.

legacy-payment-limitations.label: Payment limitations
legacy-payment-limitations.note: Cash is safest until current post-reopening policy is confirmed.

documents.name: Migiwatei Ochi Kochi
documents.summary: A rare private-bath view directly over historic Tomonoura and the Seto Inland Sea.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A rare private-bath view directly over historic Tomonoura and the Seto Inland Sea.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥80,000–130,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private outdoor bath is guaranteed in every room.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Cold-source water is reheated, terrace privacy is compromised, and the price-to-authenticity ratio is only moderate.

documents.name: Nameratoko Gorge
documents.summary: A long granite gorge of white slabs, clear pools, channels and broad sliding waterfalls in southwest Shikoku.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Strong regional discovery when approached as a gorge landscape rather than a single waterfall. Dry-to-normal water, warm-season greenery and enough time to walk beyond one viewpoint produce the best reward.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Several hours on the normal gorge outing; guided canyoning is a separate optional activity requiring legitimate operators and suitable conditions.

coverImage.alt: Clear water winding through pale granite slabs in Nameratoko Gorge.

documents.name: Horan-enya
documents.summary: An immense Matsue boat procession held only once each decade, with decorated boats, dancers and shrine ritual filling the city’s waterways.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its scale on water, rarity and deep civic participation make Horan-enya one of Japan’s most extraordinary event-only festival experiences.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The defining limitation is obvious: it is not annual. The next cycle is expected in 2029, so this is a planning overlay rather than a normally available attraction.

visit-window.note: Rare ten-year cycle; next event is expected in 2029 and exact dates should be confirmed when announced.

documents.name: Yamaroku Soy Sauce
documents.summary: The brewery is both a producer and a key node in the movement to keep giant wooden fermentation vats from disappearing.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Traditional wooden-vat soy sauce and active kioke-making revival. The recommended visit is: Take the brewery tour, inspect the vats, taste multiple ageing styles, then treat novelty sweets as secondary.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Tour often free/low cost; tasting and products extra

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Production days and tour availability vary; island transport must be planned.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Cooler fermentation season or shoulder season

legacy-english-menu.label: English menu
legacy-english-menu.note: Some English support/material may be available

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Official contact; small-group access may be flexible

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Island bus possible but car is much easier

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Do not enter production areas without staff; strong aromas and uneven floors.

documents.name: Nijigen no Mori
documents.summary: A large outdoor anime and game IP park on Awaji Island, with activity-heavy zones built around franchises such as Naruto, Dragon Quest and Crayon Shin-chan.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest attractions turn familiar IP into physical courses, missions and environments rather than relying only on character displays, making it a serious fan destination.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: anime themed park · outdoor adventure attraction

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Tickets are fragmented by attraction, the park is spread out and shade is limited in hot weather; value varies heavily with franchise interest.

visit-window.note: Outdoor heat and rain materially affect the day; reserve signature attractions in advance during busy periods.

documents.name: Niihama Taiko Festival
documents.summary: A huge autumn festival where richly embroidered taikodai floats are carried and raised by large teams in competitive kakikurabe displays.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The physical scale, embroidery and mass lifting produce one of Shikoku’s most forceful visual festival experiences.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The action is fragmented across districts and schedules, while the most dramatic confrontations can be difficult for outsiders to reach or view safely.

visit-window.note: A fixed October festival with district-specific schedules; plan the viewing sequence in advance.

documents.name: Tottori Sand Dunes Children’s Kingdom
documents.localName: アイエム電子 鳥取砂丘 こどもの国
documents.summary: A large children-first park beside the dunes combining major outdoor play with woodwork, sand craft and rotating creative activities.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Very good for families with preschool and primary-school children and worth a regional detour when travelling through Tottori. Teens and adults without children have much less reason to make a dedicated trip.

audience.notes: Purpose-built for children. Teen and adult fit is mainly as accompanying family rather than as a standalone attraction.

coverImage.alt: Entrance gate of Tottori Sand Dunes Children’s Kingdom.

documents.name: Chiburijima Island Circuit
documents.summary: A compact whole-island journey links nearly treeless pasture, cattle and horses, old stone walls, villages and oxidized red volcanic sea cliffs.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Unlike an island built around a single viewpoint, Chiburijima combines pasture history, volcanic geology and settlement in one continuous small-scale journey. It is a strong reason not to stop Oki research at Nishinoshima.

visualSignals.label: Setting
visualSignals.value: grazed volcanic upland · red sea cliffs

coverImage.alt: Documentary photograph of Chiburijima, representative of Chiburijima Island Circuit.

documents.name: Yufuin Bettei Kaze no Mori
documents.localName: 由布院別邸 風の森
documents.summary: A compact six-villa Yufuin alternative with authentic water and no need to pay the area’s highest brand premium.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A compact six-villa Yufuin alternative with authentic water and no need to pay the area’s highest brand premium.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥50,000–70,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Indoor and outdoor private baths are guaranteed in every detached unit.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Confirm that the lowest plan still includes dinner and breakfast; scenery is forest/garden rather than panoramic.

documents.name: Isamu Noguchi Garden Museum Japan
documents.localName: イサム・ノグチ庭園美術館
documents.summary: Isamu Noguchi’s preserved Mure studio and garden, where unfinished stone, working spaces and landscape reveal the sculptor’s process in situ.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The authenticity and controlled preservation of Noguchi’s working environment create exceptional depth for sculpture and design specialists despite the small scale.

booking.note: Advance reservation or ticketing is required for the core experience.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Visits are reservation-only, short and deliberately controlled, making it a specialist detour rather than a broad all-day museum.

visit-window.note: Advance reservation is mandatory and available visit slots are limited.

documents.name: Tamachan
documents.summary: The abundance of locally farmed oysters makes the griddled dish an expression of Hinase's aquaculture rather than a novelty topping.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Hinase oyster okonomiyaki using locally farmed oysters. The recommended visit is: Visit in oyster season and order the standard oyster okonomiyaki before richer variations.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Oyster season and waits matter; off-season menu may be less distinctive.

legacy-public-transport.label: Public transport practicality
legacy-public-transport.note: Possible by rail but local transport helps

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Hot griddle seating and queues; oyster availability varies.

documents.name: Konpira Kabuki
documents.summary: Annual kabuki performances inside Kanamaruza, Japan’s oldest surviving complete kabuki playhouse, using a remarkably intimate historic theatre.
documents.whyWorthwhile: The building is not merely a museum backdrop: seeing professional kabuki performed in the old proportions and stage machinery creates a specialist experience with no close modern-theatre substitute.

booking.note: Advance reservation or ticketing is required for the core experience.

coreExperience.note: Japanese materially improves interpretation or participation; arrange English support or prepare translation where practical.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Performances are limited and tickets can be difficult; Japanese language materially improves the drama even though stagecraft and atmosphere remain legible.

visit-window.note: Kabuki performances are scheduled seasonally rather than continuously; secure the exact performance before travel.

documents.name: Mitakien
documents.localName: 山菜料理 みたき園
documents.summary: The landscape, water, preserved ingredients and simple preparations form a coherent mountain meal rather than decorative rusticity.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Seasonal mountain-vegetable meal in a forest compound. The recommended visit is: Reserve a full meal and leave time to explore the compound slowly.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Seasonal operation and winter closure are likely; verify annual dates.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Uneven paths and outdoor elements; arrive prepared for weather.

documents.name: Iwami Tatamigaura
documents.summary: A broad Miocene wave-cut platform whose repeating nodules, potholes and horizontal beds become especially legible at low tide.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile for geology and unusual coastlines if timed for low tide and moderate seas. High water hides much of the pattern, so tide planning is part of the recommendation rather than a minor optimisation.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Short physical visit, but travel and tide timing are the real effort.

coverImage.alt: The exposed patterned rock platform of Iwami Tatamigaura at the coast.

documents.name: Shiseki Ryotei Kagetsu
documents.summary: Shippoku's shared-table structure and layered Chinese, Japanese and European port influences are experienced in an environment directly tied to Nagasaki's social history.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Nagasaki shippoku cuisine in a historic entertainment district setting. The recommended visit is: Reserve the complete shippoku course and ask how dishes are shared and sequenced.

visualSignals.label: Spend
visualSignals.value: Approx. ¥15,000 lunch; ¥25,000 dinner, verify current tax/service

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Full reservation required; private-room and minimum-order conditions may apply.

legacy-best-timing.label: Best timing
legacy-best-timing.note: Lunch for clearer historical visit; any season

legacy-reservation-method.label: Reservation method
legacy-reservation-method.note: Official web/phone; at least previous-day reservation reported

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Formal shared-course etiquette, punctuality and cancellation rules apply.

documents.name: Miike Coal Mine System
documents.summary: A cross-prefecture industrial landscape linking Manda and Miyanohara pits, machinery, railway traces and port infrastructure from the Miike coal system.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Taken as a coherent Omuta–Arao route, the surviving machinery and infrastructure make the scale of Japanese industrialisation far more tangible than either pit alone.

visualSignals.label: Experience
visualSignals.value: industrial heritage system · coal mining history

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese materially improves interpretation or participation; arrange English support or prepare translation where practical.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The system remains geographically fragmented and the richest guiding is often Japanese; a poorly planned visit risks reducing it to disconnected ruins.

visit-window.note: Sites have separate opening days and tour schedules; plan the full route before travel.

documents.name: Kuniga Coast
documents.summary: Pastoral uplands fall directly into immense sea cliffs, arches and stacks, with the best experience coming from walking from Matengai down toward the lower coast.
documents.whyWorthwhile: It is one of the strongest combinations found of sustained coastal walking, working pasture and vertical marine topography, and the ordinary trail delivers the same contrast seen in the famous imagery.

documents.name: Flugel Kuju
documents.localName: 久住温泉 フリューゲル久住
documents.summary: A 10-villa highland retreat with stars, mountain air, indoor/outdoor baths and strong value.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A 10-villa highland retreat with stars, mountain air, indoor/outdoor baths and strong value.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥57,000–90,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Indoor and outdoor private baths are guaranteed in every villa.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Car-oriented; bath views can be forest-framed rather than panoramic.

documents.name: Sonogi Cha Onsen Tsuwabuki no Hana
documents.localName: そのぎ茶温泉 里山の湯宿 つわぶきの花
documents.summary: A major under-recognized detached-villa value combining satoyama, authentic water and regional food.
documents.whyWorthwhile: A major under-recognized detached-villa value combining satoyama, authentic water and regional food.
cardSignals: Two: From about ¥61,600 total for two with dinner and breakfast.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Private indoor and outdoor baths are guaranteed in every unit.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Car-oriented and comparatively obscure; exact room separation and seasonal price need date-specific checks.

documents.name: Okuizumo Tatara Cultural Landscape
documents.localName: 奥出雲たたら製鉄・棚田景観
documents.summary: A rural landscape where former iron-sand extraction terrain was deliberately reworked into rice terraces, channels and productive fields.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Major-detour worthwhile for landscape/history interests, ideally as a half- or full-day car journey linking a tatara museum or furnace site with the agricultural terrain. Green rice season, harvest gold and autumn all work. The experience is weaker if treated as one viewpoint without context.

legacy-effort-required.label: Effort required
legacy-effort-required.note: Car strongly recommended; half to full day to connect dispersed landscape evidence and interpretation.

coverImage.alt: Terraced rice fields in the Okuizumo cultural landscape.

documents.name: Niimiya
documents.localName: たらいうどん 新見屋
documents.summary: The roughly 20-minute boil, shared tub and riverside setting preserve a social eating form with roots in local women's-group hospitality.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Thick communal udon served in a wooden tub with complex dipping broth. The recommended visit is: Order one communal tub sized for the group and use the wait to explore the riverside rather than adding excessive sides.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Preparation takes time; stairs and limited accessibility are material; current holidays should be checked.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Expect a long noodle-cooking wait; stair access is difficult for reduced mobility.

documents.name: Yusuhara Kengo Kuma Architecture
documents.summary: A remote mountain town containing an unusually dense group of Kengo Kuma timber buildings, including the community library, hotel and bridge museum.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Yusuhara lets visitors compare Kuma’s timber language across civic, hospitality and infrastructural projects in the landscape that shaped the work.

booking.note: Normal admission or public viewing does not require advance booking, although busy dates may still reward planning.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The town is remote and architecture-specific; transport time is substantial and individual buildings are not all long visits.

visit-window.note: The architecture is broadly year-round, but mountain-road weather and opening days should be checked.

documents.name: Kamenoi Bessou
documents.summary: Historic architecture, deep gardens, source authenticity, food and Yufuin atmosphere form a complete destination stay.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Historic architecture, deep gardens, source authenticity, food and Yufuin atmosphere form a complete destination stay.
cardSignals: Two: Approximately ¥100,000–180,000 total for two with dinner and breakfast in qualifying detached rooms.

legacy-reservation-model.label: Reservation model
legacy-reservation-model.note: Book only a detached room explicitly showing an outdoor bath.

legacy-important-caveats.label: Important caveats
legacy-important-caveats.note: Not every detached room has an outdoor bath; exact room category must be checked and rates are high.

documents.name: Kotsukotsuan
documents.summary: One practical meal can compare several Oita dishes whose names and structures would otherwise require separate searches.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Broad cross-section of Oita household and drinking dishes. The recommended visit is: Order a small regional sampler rather than treating chicken tempura alone as the destination.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Lunch and dinner formats differ; popular evenings may fill.

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Alcohol-oriented evenings; portion sizes should be checked.

documents.name: Saijo Sake Festival
documents.summary: A major annual sake festival layered onto Saijo’s working brewery district, with brewery openings, tastings, food and national sake representation.
documents.whyWorthwhile: For sake enthusiasts it turns an already strong production district into a city-scale celebration with unusually dense access to breweries and regional styles.

booking.note: Advance planning or reservation is recommended because capacity, crowds or component schedules can affect the visit.

coreExperience.note: Japanese adds context, but the core visitor experience remains understandable with limited Japanese and translation support.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: Crowding is intense and much of the experience is tasting-led rather than deep production access, so general visitors may find the festival less substantial than specialists.

visit-window.note: The 2026 festival is scheduled for 10–11 October; future dates must be reconfirmed annually.

documents.name: Yamagoe Udon
documents.summary: The freshly lifted noodles, raw egg and minimal seasoning show the technical quality of Sanuki udon with almost no disguise.
documents.whyWorthwhile: Its strongest decision-relevant feature is access to Kama-tama udon in the rural self-service Sanuki system. The recommended visit is: Order a small kama-tama and, if appetite permits, a small cold bowl to compare texture.

legacy-opening-season.label: Opening / seasonal considerations
legacy-opening-season.note: Morning/lunch only; closes when noodles sell out; holiday closures can be complex.

legacy-ordering-difficulty.label: Ordering / language friction
legacy-ordering-difficulty.note: C: self-service sequence should be learned beforehand

legacy-important-rules.label: Important rules
legacy-important-rules.note: Follow tray, topping, payment and dish-return flow; do not linger during queues.

documents.name: Izumi Crane Migration
documents.summary: One of the world’s great winter crane concentrations, when thousands of cranes gather on the agricultural plains around Izumi.
documents.whyWorthwhile: At peak season the sheer number, sound and movement of cranes transform the landscape into a natural spectacle substantial enough to justify a seasonal detour.

booking.note: Normal admission or public viewing does not require advance booking, although busy dates may still reward planning.

coreExperience.note: The core experience is primarily visual, physical or environmental and does not require Japanese.

constraint.label: Material constraint
constraint.note: The A-tier experience is seasonal and wildlife-dependent; weather, disease-management rules and yearly bird distribution can change viewing conditions.

visit-window.note: Target the winter migration season, broadly November to March, and check current wildlife-management notices.
